content: The following adverse events have been reported with varying frequencies: pulmonary alveolar hemorrhage (7-9%), gastrointestinal hemorrhage (3-9%), sepsis (5-7%), graft-versus-host disease (GVHD) (4-6%), lung infiltration (3-6%), pneumonia (3-5%), pulmonary hemorrhage (2-4%), infections (2-3%), intracranial hemorrhage (2-3%), hyperuricemia (2%), and cerebral hemorrhage (2%). Hypersensitivity reactions, including rash, urticaria, and angioedema, have been reported in less than 2% of cases. Defibrotide is contraindicated in patients with known hypersensitivity to the drug or its excipients. It increases the activity of fibrinolytic enzymes in vitro, which may elevate the risk of bleeding in patients with veno-occlusive disease (VOD). Patients should be monitored closely for signs of bleeding. The drug should not be initiated in patients with active bleeding, and if bleeding occurs, treatment should be discontinued, and the underlying cause addressed. Defibrotide should not be co-administered with systemic anticoagulants or fibrinolytic agents, except for routine maintenance or reopening of central venous lines. There is no available data on the use of defibrotide in pregnant women. Based on animal studies, pregnant women should be informed of the potential risk of miscarriage. It is unknown whether the drug is excreted in human breast milk. Due to the potential for serious adverse reactions, including bleeding in breastfed infants, breastfeeding is not recommended during treatment. The developmental and health benefits of breastfeeding should be weighed against the mother’s clinical need for the drug and any potential adverse effects on the infant from the drug or the underlying maternal condition. Unopened vials of defibrotide should be stored at 20-25°C (68-77°F), with permitted excursions between 15-30°C (59-86°F). The vials do not contain antimicrobial preservatives and are intended for single-patient use only. Partially used vials should be discarded. The diluted solution should be used within 4 hours if stored at room temperature or within 24 hours if refrigerated. Up to four doses may be prepared at one time if refrigerated. Defibrotide should not be co-administered with other intravenous drugs through the same IV line. A 9% NaCl solution should be administered immediately before and after defibrotide administration. The above information is provided for general informational and educational purposes. Individual treatment plans may vary, and formulary information is subject to change. For the most current information, contact the applicable plan provider.
